 Hon'Ble Jitendra Kumar Sinha, J. 
1. Heard Sri A.K. Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri U.S. Mishra, learned A.G.A. for
the State and perused the record.

2. The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime no. 139 of 2023
under Sections 420, 406 Ipc, Police Station Kotwali, District Bareilly with the prayer that in the
event of arrest, the applicant may be released on bail.
3.  It has been contended by learned counsel for the applicant that chargesheet has been submitted in the case under sections 420 and 406 IPC.

It is also submitted that sections 406, 420 I.P.C.,
cannot stand together in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in 'Delhi Race Club (1940)Ltd and others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another', 2024 4 ACR 610.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that applicant has filed FIR regarding theft of his tractor against some unknown persons.
It is further submitted that as per the FIR, applicant is said to have obtained loan for purchase of a tractor but he has neither repaid the loan nor returned the tractor to the bank.
It is further submitted that now the applicant has paid the entire loan amount to the bank on 04.8.2025.
It is further submitted that applicant has no criminal history to his credit.

It was also submitted that applicant undertakes to co-operate during trial and he would appear as and when required by the investigating agency or Court and in case he is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.
4. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail.
5. I have considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.
6. Chargesheet has been submitted in the case and the applicant is said to have paid the entire loan amount to the bank on 04.8.2025.

7. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, the Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedents of the accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate the entire available material against the accused carefully and the exact role of accused has also to be taken into consideration.

Considering all attending facts and circumstances of the case, settled principle of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicants and without expressing any opinion on merits, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.

9. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
10.
